issues.title: Test comment wrongly says the no-fix failure manifests as the ~output_stream() assert
issues.verdictReason: test_data_sink_impl::put() (rpc_test.cc:1884-1888) forwards synchronously to _inner.put(), so the late write completes; the yield loop at rpc_test.cc:2022-2024 then lets the batch-flush poller finish before sink/source are dropped, so _in_batch is false by destruction time and the assert the comment describes would not fire — the actual no-fix signal is BOOST_REQUIRE_MESSAGE(!st.put_after_close) at line 2030, matching the PR body's own more careful wording.
issues.scopeReason: The comment is new test code added by this PR.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr2: Test comment misattributes failure mode to assertion instead of BOOST_REQUIRE

reportedAsByRun.opus-5-5-review-and-fix-pr2-r43-2026-10-: The test comment at rpc_test.cc:2031-2033 says that without the fix, ~output_stream() asserts, but the wrapper's put() forwards to _inner.put() (line 1887), so the late write is flushed and the real failure without the fix is the BOOST_REQUIRE_MESSAGE at line 2030, not the assertion. The PR body itself correctly states the assertion only happens if the late put() is left unresolved.

issues.title: New doc text understates that dropping an unclosed sink aborts the process
issues.verdictReason: sink_impl::~sink_impl() runs SEASTAR_ASSERT(this->_con->get()->sink_closed()) (include/seastar/rpc/rpc_impl.hh:933-935), and SEASTAR_ASSERT calls assert_fail(), which is [[noreturn]] and aborts the process — calling an unclosed sink drop 'an error' understates that this is a process-killing bug, not a recoverable exception.
issues.scopeReason: This sentence is new documentation added by this PR's 'Closing a stream' section.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr2: Docs understate that dropping an unclosed sink aborts the process

reportedAsByRun.opus-5-5-review-and-fix-pr2-r43-2026-10-: The doc statement 'Dropping an unclosed sink is an error' (rpc-streaming.md:109) reads like a recoverable error, but ~sink_impl runs SEASTAR_ASSERT(...sink_closed()) (rpc_impl.hh:935) which aborts the process.

issues.title: New doc text wrongly claims connection shuts down only once both stream halves close
issues.verdictReason: The same PR's own lines 48-50 say closing the client aborts any open stream, and client::abort_all_streams() (src/rpc/rpc.cc:848, called at rpc.cc:1072 and rpc.cc:1295) plus connection::abort() (rpc.cc:346) tear a stream connection down on error paths without both halves ever being orderly-closed; the absolute 'only once both halves are closed' sentence is true solely for the graceful path.
issues.scopeReason: This sentence is new documentation added by this PR's 'Closing a stream' section.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr2: Doc overstates that the stream's connection shuts down only when both halves close

reportedAsByRun.opus-5-5-review-and-fix-pr2-r43-2026-10-: The claim 'The stream's connection is shut down only once both halves are closed' (rpc-streaming.md:115) contradicts the doc's own lines 49-50, which say closing the client aborts the stream, and ignores that abort() on a send failure, read errors, and client::abort_all_streams() (rpc.cc ~line 1072) also shut the connection down earlier. The sentence only holds for an orderly close.

issues.title: New comment overstates that nothing else waits on _outgoing_queue_ready
issues.verdictReason: stop_send_loop() (rpc.cc:225) does reference the _outgoing_queue_ready member in a when_all; the comment is only true because the preceding std::exchange (rpc.cc:562) has already replaced that member with a ready placeholder, a detail the comment omits.
issues.scopeReason: The comment and the code it describes are new in this PR.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr2: Comment claims nothing waits on _outgoing_queue_ready when stop_send_loop still does

reportedAsByRun.opus-5-5-review-and-fix-pr2-r43-2026-10-: The comment 'Nothing else waits for _outgoing_queue_ready from here on' (rpc.cc:559-561) is not literally true: stop_send_loop() still runs when_all(std::move(_outgoing_queue_ready), ...) (rpc.cc:225). The wait is harmless only because of the ready placeholder std::exchange installs at line 562, which the comment should state.

issues.title: New test's condition-variable wait has no timeout and can stall to the harness limit
issues.verdictReason: condition_variable::wait(pred) used here has no deadline, while the class does support a timed wait (condition_variable_timed_out in include/seastar/core/condition-variable.hh); if stream_close() never reaches data_sink::close() the test stalls until the external 300s test-runner timeout rather than failing with a specific message, which is a real but minor diagnosability gap rather than a functional bug.
issues.scopeReason: This wait is new code in the test this PR adds.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr2: Test's condition-variable wait has no deadline and can hang until harness timeout

reportedAsByRun.opus-5-5-review-and-fix-pr2-r43-2026-10-: close_entered_cv.wait(pred) at rpc_test.cc:2011 is unbounded. If stream_close() never reaches data_sink::close(), the test hangs until the 300s harness timeout instead of failing with a clear error.

issues.title: Any early failure in the new test aborts the whole test process via the unclosed sink's…
issues.verdictReason: sink is a local created before BOOST_REQUIRE_EQUAL at line 2000; sink_impl::~sink_impl() (include/seastar/rpc/rpc_impl.hh:933-935) asserts sink_closed() and SEASTAR_ASSERT aborts the process, so any BOOST_REQUIRE failure or thrown exception before sink.close() completes kills the whole test binary (masking the real failure and any other tests in the run) instead of reporting a clean test failure; the 'hangs' half of the original claim does not hold because the sink's LIFO-first destructor aborts before shared_promise's broken-promise teardown could ever stall anything, but the core robustness gap is real.
issues.scopeReason: This is new test code with no cleanup guard added by this PR.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr2: Test cleanup is skipped if anything fails part-way, causing an abort or a hang

reportedAsByRun.opus-5-5-review-and-fix-pr2-r43-2026-10-: If BOOST_REQUIRE_EQUAL at line 2000 fails, or anything throws before the sink is closed, the unwind drops an unclosed sink, tripping the rpc_impl.hh:935 assert so the process aborts instead of reporting the test failure. Separately, if anything throws between lines 2011 and 2026, release_close.set_value() never runs, so the parked close, sink_closed, and server_done futures never resolve and teardown hangs. A defer that releases the close and drains both futures would fix both hazards.

issues.title: Test never directly asserts the refused frame throws closed_error
issues.verdictReason: The try/catch at rpc_test.cc:2016-2020 swallows both the success and closed_error outcomes without failing either way, so the fix's documented contract (send() fails with closed_error once stream_close() has begun) is only indirectly checked via the later BOOST_REQUIRE_MESSAGE(!st.put_after_close); a BOOST_REQUIRE_THROW would check the contract directly, though the existing assertion still catches the regression this test targets.
issues.scopeReason: This is new test code added by this PR.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr2: Test never asserts the refused frame actually throws closed_error

reportedAsByRun.opus-5-5-review-and-fix-pr2-r43-2026-10-: The try/catch at rpc_test.cc:2016-2020 accepts both success and closed_error, so the fix's actual contract that send() fails with closed_error is never checked; the test relies only on put_after_close. BOOST_REQUIRE_THROW(..., rpc::closed_error) would check it directly.

issues.title: New test never exercises the queue-drain wait branch or the server-side stream hook
issues.verdictReason: In the test, sink(1).get() is awaited to completion and the source is drained to eof before sink.close() runs stream_close(), so _outgoing_queue_ready is already a ready future by the time std::exchange runs at rpc.cc:562, leaving the queue-drain wait and its then_wrapped exceptional-swallow path (rpc.cc:566-569) untested, and server_factory's hooks (rpc_test.cc:1966/1970) are never invoked or asserted against.
issues.scopeReason: The untested branch is new code this PR added, and the test that should cover it is also new.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr2: Queue-drain wait branch and server-side stream hook are never exercised by the test

reportedAsByRun.opus-5-5-review-and-fix-pr2-r43-2026-10-: The eof frame is already awaited before close_sink() runs, so queue_drained is always ready in this test, leaving the wait-for-queued-entries branch and the exceptional then_wrapped swallow path (rpc.cc:562-569) untested. Also, server_factory captures hooks that are never invoked or asserted, so the server-side stream connection (rpc.cc:1103, test at rpc_test.cc:1966/:2001) has no stimulus.

issues.title: New source doc comment overstates that there is no other way to release a source
issues.verdictReason: source_impl has no destructor assertion analogous to sink_impl's, and the PR's own new text at doc/rpc-streaming.md:49-50 says closing or aborting the client tears down any open stream including its source, so an application can in fact end up with a torn-down source without ever reading it to eof or a throw; 'no other way to do it' is an overstatement of the intended usage contract.
issues.scopeReason: This doc comment is new text added by this PR.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr2: Doc comment wrongly claims there is no other way to tear down the source

reportedAsByRun.opus-5-5-review-and-fix-pr2-r43-2026-10-: The statement 'there is no other way to do it' (rpc_types.hh:386-387) is inaccurate because closing or aborting the client also tears the source down, as the new doc text at rpc-streaming.md:49 itself states.

issues.title: Pre-existing _sink_closed_future comment is now less precise given the new queue-drain…
issues.verdictReason: The comment ('if it is not ready it means the sink is been closed') is pre-existing and still factually true, but this PR's queue-drain wait (src/rpc/rpc.cc:562-569) added a new phase to that not-ready window that the comment doesn't mention, making it a looser description than before.
issues.scopeReason: The PR's own change to stream_close() is what widened the window this adjacent comment describes.

issues.title: Fix commit lands before its regression test, in a separate commit
issues.verdictReason: Splitting a fix commit from its regression-test commit is a normal, common pattern (including in Linux-kernel-style workflows this repo's own contributing.md patterns itself on); both commits build and the two together are trivial to backport as a pair, so no concrete maintenance hazard is demonstrated beyond ordinary practice.
issues.scopeReason: This is a stylistic preference about commit organization, not a defect the PR introduced into the codebase.

issues.title: _stream_closing is only consulted by send(), not by error()/sink_closed()
issues.verdictReason: connection::send() (src/rpc/rpc.cc:293) is the only reader of _stream_closing; error() (rpc.hh:340) and sink_closed() (rpc.hh:353) don't see it, so any future send-like code path that guards itself with error() instead of calling send() directly would miss the closing window — a real but currently-hypothetical coupling risk, not an active bug since no such path exists today.
issues.scopeReason: _stream_closing is a new field this PR introduced.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr2: New _stream_closing flag is checked only in send(), not in error() or sink_closed()

reportedAsByRun.opus-5-5-review-and-fix-pr2-r43-2026-10-: _stream_closing (rpc.hh:307) is checked only in send() (rpc.cc:293); error() and sink_closed() ignore it, so a future send-like path guarded by error() would miss the closing window. A single closing() predicate would avoid that.

issues.scopeReason: This loop is new test code added by this PR.
